The new house next door was quiet for months. Lin's mother told her that an old lady called Grandma Heng had moved in after her husband died. One Saturday, Lin brought over a plate of her mother's steamed buns. Grandma Heng opened the door slowly and smiled. Soon, Lin began to visit every afternoon. She read her school books aloud while the old lady knitted by the window.

Grandma Heng had many stories. She told Lin about the town when it was small, with rice fields where the flats now stood. Lin sketched these tales in her exercise book. By the end of the term, the two of them had made a small book together. Lin's mother watched and said nothing, but she often sent extra food next door. Lin learnt that a lonely person did not need grand gifts. A visitor, a kind word, and time were enough.


What did Lin bring Grandma Heng on her first visit?
questions.explanation: Paragraph one says Lin brought over a plate of her mother's steamed buns.

questions.questionText: The telephone ______; please answer it before it stops ringing.
questions.explanation: A phone ringing right now shows an action in progress, so we use the present continuous: is ringing.

questions.questionText: Look at the sky! It ______ heavily right now.
questions.explanation: 'Right now' shows the action is in progress now, so we use is raining.

questions.questionText: At the moment, my father ______ dinner in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: 'At the moment' is a present-continuous time marker, so we use is cooking.

questions.questionText: I cannot play now because I ______ for a test.
questions.explanation: 'Now' shows an action in progress; with 'I' the present continuous is am studying.

questions.questionText: Listen! Someone ______ the piano next door.
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' signals an action happening at this moment, so we use is playing.

questions.questionText: At eight o'clock last night, we ______ television.
questions.explanation: 'At eight o'clock last night' is a point of time in the past, so we use the past continuous: were watching.

questions.questionText: While Mum ______ up, the children set the table for dinner.
questions.explanation: 'While' introduces a longer background action in the past, so we use was washing.

questions.questionText: When the storm began, the fishermen ______ back to the shore.
questions.explanation: 'When the storm began' interrupts an ongoing past action, so the background action uses were heading.

questions.questionText: I met Mr Lee yesterday. He ______ his bicycle along the park road.
questions.explanation: The second clause describes an action in progress when I saw him, so we use was riding.

questions.questionText: This time last year, my family ______ in a small flat by the sea.
questions.explanation: 'This time last year' points to an ongoing state at a past moment, so we use were living.

questions.questionText: ______ is that man standing near the school gate?
questions.explanation: We use 'Who' to ask about the identity of a person.

questions.questionText: ______ did you buy for your mother's birthday?
questions.explanation: We use 'What' to ask about a thing.

questions.questionText: ______ umbrella is dripping water on the floor?
questions.explanation: We use 'Whose' to ask who something belongs to.

questions.questionText: ______ subject do you like better, Art or Music?
questions.explanation: With a limited choice (Art or Music) we use 'Which'.

questions.questionText: ______ won the 100-metre race yesterday?

questions.questionText: To ______ should I send the invitation card?
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'to' the object form is 'whom'.

questions.questionText: ______ is the lady talking to our English teacher?
questions.explanation: We use 'Who' to ask the identity of the person (subject of the clause).

questions.questionText: ______ do you think the judges chose as the winner?
questions.explanation: Insert 'do you think' aside: the judges chose [him/her], so the object form 'Whom' is correct.

questions.questionText: Which of these is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: Bread is an uncountable noun; we say 'a loaf/slice of bread', not 'one bread'.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a countable noun?
questions.explanation: Grape is countable (one grape, two grapes); rice, water and milk are uncountable.

questions.questionText: There is not ______ milk left in the jug.
questions.explanation: Milk is uncountable; in a negative sentence we use 'any milk'.

questions.questionText: We need to buy ______ rice this week.
questions.explanation: Rice is uncountable, so we use 'some rice', not 'a rice' or 'many rice'.

questions.questionText: There is too ______ noise in the canteen at recess.
questions.explanation: Noise is uncountable, so we use 'much'.

questions.questionText: Can I have ______ water, please? I am thirsty.
questions.explanation: Water is uncountable, so we use 'some water'.

questions.questionText: There are too ______ cars on the road today.
questions.explanation: Cars are countable (plural), so we use 'many'.

questions.questionText: Which of these words is always an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: Furniture is uncountable; the others are countable items.

questions.questionText: There are four ______ in the fruit basket.
questions.explanation: Mango is a regular countable noun; the plural is 'mangoes'.

questions.questionText: I brush my ______ every morning and at night.
questions.explanation: The plural of 'tooth' is the irregular form 'teeth'.

questions.questionText: Mum keeps two sharp ______ in the kitchen drawer.
questions.explanation: 'Knife' has the irregular plural 'knives'.

questions.questionText: Dad bought three ______ of rice for the family.
questions.explanation: 'Kilo' is a regular countable noun; the plural is 'kilos'.

questions.questionText: There is not ______ information about the trip on the notice board.
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable, so we use 'much information'.

questions.questionText: The teacher gave us ______ homework to finish tonight.
questions.explanation: Homework is uncountable, so we use 'a lot of homework', not 'many homework'.

questions.questionText: We spotted several ______ near the lake in the park.
questions.explanation: 'Deer' has the same form in the plural: 'several deer'.

questions.questionText: A farmer kept six white ______ on his pond.
questions.explanation: The plural of 'goose' is the irregular form 'geese'.

questions.questionText: Please do not make so ______ noise; the baby is asleep.
questions.explanation: Noise is uncountable, so we use 'much noise'.

questions.questionText: Three ______ in blue caps are fixing the school roof.
questions.explanation: The plural of 'man' is the irregular form 'men'.

questions.questionText: Can you give me ______ paper? I need to write a quick note.
questions.explanation: Paper (material) is uncountable; we count it as 'a piece of paper'.

questions.questionText: The librarian gave me useful ______ on choosing my books.
questions.explanation: Advice is uncountable; it has no plural and cannot take 'an'.

questions.questionText: There are only ______ bananas left, not enough for everyone.
questions.explanation: Bananas are countable, so we use 'a few'.

questions.questionText: We have ______ time before the bus leaves, so please do not rush.
questions.explanation: Time is uncountable, so we use 'plenty of time'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence about 'equipment'.

options.label: A
options.text: The equipment in the science lab is new

options.label: B
options.text: The equipments in the science lab are new

options.label: C
options.text: An equipment in the science lab is new

options.label: D
options.text: The equipment in the science lab are new

questions.explanation: Equipment is uncountable and takes a singular verb: 'the equipment ... is new'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence about 'furniture'.

options.label: A
options.text: We bought some new furniture last week

options.label: B
options.text: We bought some new furnitures last week

options.label: C
options.text: We bought a new furniture last week

options.label: D
options.text: We bought three furnitures last week

questions.explanation: Furniture is uncountable: 'some new furniture', never 'furnitures' or 'a furniture'.

questions.questionText: The news about the rescued hikers ______ good, so everyone smiled.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb: 'the news is good'.

questions.questionText:
It was raining cats and dogs when we left school, so we waited under the school eaves.

In the sentence, 'raining cats and dogs' means

options.label: A
options.text: animals were falling from the sky

questions.explanation: The idiom describes very heavy rain; the children waiting under the eaves shows it was pouring.

questions.questionText:
Do not worry about your first solo. For someone as well practised as you, it will be a piece of cake.

A 'piece of cake' means
questions.explanation: Because she is well practised, the task will be easy; 'a piece of cake' means very easy.

questions.questionText:
Grandfather only visits us once in a blue moon, usually about every two years.

'Once in a blue moon' means
questions.explanation: About every two years shows the visits happen very rarely.

questions.questionText:
Jia Hui was under the weather today, so she went home early to rest.

'Under the weather' means
questions.explanation: Going home early to rest shows she was feeling ill.

questions.questionText:
When my brother said he had eaten my lunch, I knew he was pulling my leg, because I could still see it in the fridge.

'Pulling my leg' means
questions.explanation: The lunch was still in the fridge, so his claim was a joke: 'pulling my leg' means joking.

questions.questionText:
When Tashia heard she had won the art prize, she was on cloud nine all afternoon.

'On cloud nine' means
questions.explanation: Winning a prize and feeling wonderful all afternoon shows she was extremely happy.

questions.questionText:
A brand-new bicycle like that costs an arm and a leg, so I must save up for many months.

'Costs an arm and a leg' means
questions.explanation: Saving for many months shows the bicycle is very expensive.

questions.questionText:
At the end of the day, what matters most is that we all tried our best.

'At the end of the day' means
questions.explanation: It means 'when all is considered / ultimately', not literally at sunset.

questions.questionText:
Losing that match was a blessing in disguise, because it made the team practise much harder and win the next one.

'A blessing in disguise' means

options.label: C
options.text: something bad that later turns out good

questions.explanation: The loss felt bad at first, but it led to harder practice and a later win: good hidden inside a setback.

questions.questionText:
Stop beating around the bush and tell me plainly what happened while I was away.

'Beating around the bush' means
questions.explanation: The speaker wants a direct answer, so 'beating around the bush' means avoiding the point.

questions.questionText:
Jia Hui held up a dripping wet umbrella and shook rain off her shoes. The bus was running ten minutes late.

What will probably happen next?

options.label: A
options.text: She will wait for the bus under shelter

options.label: B
options.text: She will run all the way home in the rain

options.label: C
options.text: She will buy a new umbrella at once

options.label: D
options.text: She will start to sing aloud

questions.explanation: She is already sheltering from the rain and the bus is coming, so she will wait under cover.

questions.questionText:
Sufian opened his pencil case and looked inside. His sharpener was missing. He walked towards the teacher's table.

What will probably happen next?

options.label: B
options.text: He will ask to borrow a sharpener

options.label: C
options.text: He will throw away his pencils

questions.explanation: He needs a sharpener and is going to the teacher, so he will ask to borrow one.

questions.questionText:
The school bell rang. All the pupils pushed their chairs back and stood up.

What will probably happen next?

options.label: A
options.text: They will sit down again at once

options.label: B
options.text: They will start a surprise test

options.label: C
options.text: They will leave the classroom for recess

options.label: D
options.text: They will switch off all the lights

questions.explanation: The bell at the end of a period means the pupils leave for recess.

questions.questionText:
Zi Ling put on her swimsuit, walked to the pool edge and took a deep breath.

What will probably happen next?

options.label: D
options.text: She will jump into the pool

questions.explanation: Swimsuit, pool edge and a deep breath show she is about to dive in.

questions.questionText:
The sky grew dark, the wind picked up, and thunder rumbled far away.

What will probably happen next?

options.label: C
options.text: The day will get much hotter

options.label: D
options.text: The birds will start to sing

questions.explanation: Dark sky, wind and thunder all point to rain coming.

questions.questionText:
Kah Fai plugged in the electric kettle and waited. A minute later, it clicked itself off.

What will probably happen next?

options.label: A
options.text: He will drink cold water instead

options.label: B
options.text: He will switch the kettle on again

options.label: C
options.text: He will go outside for a walk

options.label: D
options.text: He will pour the hot water into a cup

questions.explanation: The kettle boiled and clicked off, so the next step is pouring the hot water.

questions.questionText:
The cook put the cake tin in the oven and set the kitchen timer.

What will the cook probably do next?

options.label: A
options.text: Wait for the timer to ring

questions.explanation: After setting a timer you wait for it to ring before checking the cake.

questions.questionText:
Nurul picked up her broom and swept the fallen leaves into a pile on the path.

What will she probably do next?

options.label: A
options.text: Leave them lying on the ground

options.label: B
options.text: Water the leaves with a hose

options.label: C
options.text: Collect the leaves into a dustbin

questions.explanation: Sweeping leaves into a pile is done so they can be gathered into a bin.

questions.questionText:
An old man crossed slowly at the zebra crossing. All the drivers had stopped and were waiting.

What will the drivers probably do?

options.label: B
options.text: Wait until he reaches the pavement

questions.explanation: At a zebra crossing drivers wait until pedestrians reach the other side.

questions.questionText:
Tashia opened her umbrella as dark clouds began to gather overhead.

What was the weather about to do?
questions.explanation: Dark clouds and opening an umbrella show rain is coming.

questions.questionText:
First, Sufian broke two eggs into a bowl. Next, he added flour and stirred it well. Then he poured in some milk.

What did Sufian do just before he poured in the milk?

options.label: A
options.text: He stirred the flour and eggs

questions.explanation: The order given is: eggs, then flour-and-stir, then milk - so he stirred just before adding milk.

questions.questionText:
We walked to the bus stop, took the bus into town, and then walked to the museum.

Where did we go first?
questions.explanation: The first step in the order is walking to the bus stop.

questions.questionText:
Jia Hui finished her homework, then she fed the cat, and after that she set the table for dinner.

What did Jia Hui do right after she finished her homework?
questions.explanation: The order is homework -> fed the cat -> set the table, so feeding the cat came right after homework.

questions.questionText:
Before it started to rain, the children had flown their kite in the open field. When the first big drop fell, they ran to the car.

What did the children do as soon as it began to rain?
questions.explanation: The sentence says: when the first drop fell, they ran to the car.

questions.questionText:
The farmer ploughed the field, then he sowed the seeds, and weeks later the green shoots came up through the soil.

What happened last?
questions.explanation: The sequence ends with the shoots coming up weeks later.

questions.questionText:
Vishnu slipped on the wet floor. He sat up slowly and rubbed his knee. A teacher hurried over to him.

What will probably happen next?

options.label: A
options.text: The teacher will scold him loudly

options.label: D
options.text: The teacher will help him up and check his knee

questions.explanation: A teacher hurrying to a child who fell will help him and check the injury.

questions.questionText:
The bread came out of the oven. When the timer rang, Nurul pulled it out and touched it; it was still soft and raw inside.

What will Nurul probably do next?

options.label: B
options.text: Put it back in the oven a little longer

options.label: D
options.text: Turn the oven to the highest heat

questions.explanation: Raw inside means it needs more baking time.

questions.questionText:
Kah Fai had saved his pocket money for many months. At last he held the box he had been waiting so long to buy.

What will Kah Fai probably do next?

options.label: D
options.text: Open the box and see his new item

questions.explanation: After saving up for a wanted item, he will open the box to see it.

questions.questionText:
The shopkeeper noticed a boy hiding a chocolate bar inside his school shirt.

What will the shopkeeper probably do?

options.label: A
options.text: Speak to the boy about what he did

questions.explanation: A shopkeeper will first speak to the pupil about taking the item.

questions.questionText:
The pupils planted a small tree by the gate, watered it well, and fixed a wooden sign into the soil beside it.

Why did they probably put up the sign?

options.label: B
options.text: To show who planted it and to care for it

questions.explanation: A sign by a new tree names the planters and reminds people to look after it.

questions.questionText:
Tashia practised the piano every single evening. On concert day her hands were steady and the music sounded smooth.

What does this show about Tashia?

options.label: A
options.text: She was just lucky on the day

options.label: C
options.text: Regular practice helped her play well

options.label: D
options.text: She did not need to practise

questions.explanation: The evening practice led to a steady, smooth performance: practice paid off.

questions.questionText:
Zi Ling left her bag on the bus. When she reached school, she patted her pockets and looked worried.

What will Zi Ling probably do next?

options.label: B
options.text: Go back or phone about the lost bag

options.label: C
options.text: Buy a new bag at once

questions.explanation: Realising her bag is on the bus, she will act to recover it.

questions.questionText:
The river level had risen all week. On Saturday the banks overflowed and water spread across the nearby field. The villagers carried their chickens to higher ground.

What will the villagers probably do next?

options.label: B
options.text: Move their belongings upstairs and wait for help

options.label: C
options.text: Build a small boat for fun

questions.explanation: Flooding means protecting belongings and waiting for assistance.

questions.questionText:
The old library books had turned yellow, and the pages felt damp. A teacher opened all the windows and placed an electric fan near the shelf.

Why did the teacher open the windows and use a fan?

options.label: A
options.text: To dry out the damp pages

options.label: C
options.text: To let more children into the room

questions.explanation: Damp pages need air movement to dry; the fan and windows are aimed at the shelf.

questions.questionText:
Every evening a stray dog waited at the same corner. The children left it a little rice. Slowly, it began to walk closer to them.

What will probably happen next?

options.label: A
options.text: The dog will suddenly bite them

options.label: B
options.text: The children will chase it away

options.label: C
options.text: The dog will trust the children more and may stay

questions.explanation: Small acts of care build trust, so the dog will grow closer rather than turn hostile.

questions.questionText:
The students were furious when someone had torn their group poster. They shouted and refused to leave quietly.

The word 'furious' means
questions.explanation: Shouting and refusing to leave show they were very angry.

questions.questionText:
Please handle that vase with great care. It is fragile and will break if you drop it.

The word 'fragile' means
questions.explanation: The second clause says it breaks if dropped, so it is easily broken.

questions.questionText:
Anxious about her first solo speech, Tashia twisted her hands and kept swallowing hard.

The word 'anxious' means
questions.explanation: Twisting her hands shows nervous worry.

questions.questionText:
Our generous neighbour gave biscuits she had baked to everyone living on the same floor.

The word 'generous' means
questions.explanation: Giving her own baking to everyone shows she likes to share.

questions.questionText:
The enormous elephant was so tall that it could barely walk beneath the low branches.

The word 'enormous' means
questions.explanation: Barely fitting under low branches shows it is extremely large.

questions.questionText:
When the teacher said the field trip had been put off, the whole class looked relieved.

The word 'relieved' means
questions.explanation: Putting off a feared trip lifted their worry, so they looked relieved.

questions.questionText:
The curious kitten peered into the shoebox to see what might be moving inside.

The word 'curious' means
questions.explanation: Peering to see what is inside shows a wish to know.

questions.questionText:
The old wooden bench was sturdy after years outside; it never shook even when four of us sat down together.

The word 'sturdy' means
questions.explanation: It never shook under four people, so it is strong and well-built.

questions.questionText:
We wandered through the old town with no map, turning down any narrow lane that looked interesting.

The word 'wandered' means
questions.explanation: No map and choosing lanes by interest show aimless walking.

questions.questionText:
Sufian hesitated before knocking, unsure whether he should really enter the headmaster's room.

The word 'hesitated' means
questions.explanation: Unsure whether to enter means he paused uncertainly.

questions.questionText:
Caught in the sudden storm, the hikers were drenched and their shirts clung to their backs.

The word 'drenched' means
questions.explanation: Shirts clinging to their backs after a storm means completely wet.

questions.questionText:
After the long climb up the steep hill, the exhausted children could barely stand up.

The word 'exhausted' means
questions.explanation: Barely able to stand after a long climb shows great tiredness.

questions.questionText:
The puzzled tourist looked at the map again and again, but still could not find the street.

The word 'puzzled' means
questions.explanation: Re-checking the map without success shows confusion.

questions.questionText:
Grandma kept her wedding ring in a locked wooden box; it was the most precious thing she owned.

The word 'precious' means
questions.explanation: Kept locked away, it is of great personal value.

questions.questionText:
The warm, quiet room and the soft armchair made him feel drowsy, and his eyes began to close.

The word 'drowsy' means
questions.explanation: His eyes closing in the warm room shows he was getting sleepy.

questions.questionText: The baby ______ in the next room, so please do not wake her up.
questions.explanation: The clue is 'do not wake her up' — the action is in progress right now, so we use the present continuous: is sleeping.

questions.questionText: Be careful! The big dog ______ loudly at the front gate.
questions.explanation: Right now the dog is in the middle of barking, so the present continuous is barking.

questions.questionText: Shh! The librarian ______ the returned books behind the desk.
questions.explanation: The hushed 'Shh!' tells us the action is happening now, so we use is sorting.

questions.questionText: Hurry up! It ______ darker, and the park will close soon.
questions.explanation: The sky is in the process of getting dark now, so the present continuous is getting.

questions.questionText: At three o'clock yesterday afternoon, our class ______ on the school field.
questions.explanation: A fixed time in the past ('three o'clock yesterday') describes an action already in progress, so we use were running.

questions.questionText: I met a neighbour this morning. She ______ a basket of vegetables from the market.
questions.explanation: When I saw her, the carrying was already in progress — a background past action — so we use was carrying.

questions.questionText: This time yesterday, my cousins ______ in the hotel pool.
questions.explanation: 'This time yesterday' is a past moment; the swimming was under way then, so we use were swimming.

questions.questionText: While the singer ______, the audience listened quietly.
questions.explanation: The listening happened during the singing, so the longer background action uses was singing.

questions.questionText: As I ______ along the riverbank, I suddenly saw a small snake in the grass.
questions.explanation: Seeing the snake interrupted my walk; the walk was the ongoing background action, so we use the past continuous was walking.

questions.questionText: The lights went out while we ______ a play on the school stage.
questions.explanation: The blackout interrupted a past activity, so the rehearsal is the ongoing background action: were rehearsing.

questions.questionText: My uncle hurt his hand while he ______ the old wooden fence.
questions.explanation: The injury happened during the painting, so the longer action uses the past continuous was painting.

questions.questionText: When the bell rang, the children ______ noisily in the corridor.
questions.explanation: The bell interrupted the children's conversation, so the background chatter uses were chatting.

questions.questionText: As we ______ up the hill, it suddenly began to rain.
questions.explanation: The rain began during our climb, so the climbing is the ongoing past background action: were climbing.

questions.questionText: I ______ my homework when the doorbell suddenly rang.
questions.explanation: The doorbell interrupted an action already under way, so the background action uses was doing.

questions.questionText: Look! The workmen ______ the broken road outside our house.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' shows an action in progress now, so the present continuous are repairing is correct.

questions.questionText: Grandma is in her room; she ______ her old favourite songs.
questions.explanation: Right now Grandma is in the middle of humming, so we use the present continuous is humming.

questions.questionText: Last Sunday at noon, we ______ through the busy night market.
questions.explanation: A fixed past moment describes an action already in progress, so we use were wandering.

questions.questionText: My hands are dirty because I ______ in the garden.
questions.explanation: The digging is happening now and explains why my hands are dirty, so we use am digging.

questions.questionText: The pupils ______ excitedly when the guest teacher walked in.
questions.explanation: The teacher's arrival interrupted the pupils' chatter, so the background action uses were talking.

questions.questionText: Look! The little boy ______ after the runaway balloon.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' marks an action in progress now, so the present continuous is chasing is correct.

questions.questionText: ______ it was raining heavily, the football match continued.
questions.explanation: Rain would normally stop a match, so continuing shows a contrast — we use Although.

questions.questionText: ______ you have finished eating, please clear the table.
questions.explanation: The second clause gives a reason that starts 'now that you are finished', so we use Since.

questions.questionText: The little girl went to school ______ she had a slight fever.
questions.explanation: A fever would usually keep a child home, so going to school shows contrast — we use although.

questions.questionText: ______ the traffic was terrible, we arrived at the cinema on time.
questions.explanation: Bad traffic would normally make us late, so arriving on time is a contrast — we use Although.

questions.questionText: ______ you are my best friend, I will tell you a secret.
questions.explanation: Being a trusted friend is the reason for telling the secret, so we use Since.

questions.questionText: ______ it was already late, the children did not want to go home.
questions.explanation: Being late would normally make children leave, so staying is a contrast — we use Although.

questions.questionText: My uncle has worked at the bakery ______ he left school.
questions.explanation: Here since marks the starting point in time of an action that still continues, so we use since.

questions.questionText: ______ the hotel was very expensive, many tourists still stayed there.
questions.explanation: A high price would usually put guests off, so the contrast is marked by Although.

questions.questionText: We decided to walk home ______ the last bus had already gone.
questions.explanation: The lost bus is the reason we walked, so the causal sense uses since.

questions.questionText: ______ my grandfather is seventy, he climbs the hill every day.
questions.explanation: Age would normally slow a person down, so daily climbing is a contrast — we use Although.

questions.questionText: ______ I moved to this town, I have made many new friends.
questions.explanation: Since introduces the time point from which the friendship began and continues, so we use Since.

questions.questionText: ______ she practised every day, she did not win the singing contest.
questions.explanation: Daily practice would normally lead to winning, so losing is a contrast — we use Although.

questions.questionText: Take an umbrella ______ the sky looks dark and cloudy.
questions.explanation: The cloudy sky is the reason to take an umbrella, so the causal sense uses since.

questions.questionText: The children kept playing outside ______ the wind blew strongly.
questions.explanation: Strong wind would usually drive children indoors, so staying outside is a contrast — although.

questions.questionText: ______ you have already seen the film, you can tell me how it ends.
questions.explanation: Having seen the film is the reason you can explain the ending, so we use Since.

questions.questionText: We felt quite cheerful ______ it was a cold, grey morning.
questions.explanation: A cold grey morning would normally feel gloomy, so feeling cheerful is a contrast — although.

questions.questionText: ______ the rain had stopped, the ground was still soaking wet.
questions.explanation: Stopped rain would normally leave dry ground, so the wet ground is unexpected — we use Although.

questions.questionText: The team cheered loudly ______ they had lost the match.
questions.explanation: Losing would normally make a team quiet, so cheering is a contrast — we use although.

questions.questionText: ______ everyone knew the plan was risky, they still agreed to try it.
questions.explanation: Knowing a plan is risky would normally stop it, so agreeing is a contrast — we use Although.

questions.questionText: We have known each other ______ we were in primary one.
questions.explanation: Since introduces the clause that gives the time start of the friendship; 'for' would need a noun phrase, not a clause, so since is correct.

questions.questionText: The bank is ______ the post office, on the same side of the street.
questions.explanation: Resting at the side of the post office uses beside.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: My house is ______ the small market, so I can walk there in two minutes.
questions.explanation: A two-minute walk shows closeness without touching, so we use near.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The ball rolled ______ the table and the wall, where we could not reach it.
questions.explanation: The ball is in the space separating the table and the wall, so we use between.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The bookshop is ______ the cafe; they share the same wall.
questions.explanation: Sharing a wall means immediately adjacent, so we use next to.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: Come and sit ______ me; I want to show you my drawings.
questions.explanation: Sitting immediately at the speaker's side uses next to.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The school is ______ the bus stop, just a short walk away.
questions.explanation: A short walk places the school close to but not touching the stop, so near.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: A thin layer of dust lay ______ all the old furniture in the attic.
questions.explanation: The dust covers the surface above the furniture, so we use over.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The gift shop is ______ the bakery and the bookshop.
questions.explanation: Positioned in the middle of two things uses between.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: My deskmate sits ______ me in class, on my left.
questions.explanation: The deskmate is immediately beside the speaker, so we use next to.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The cat jumped ______ the low wall into the neighbour's garden.
questions.explanation: Jumping across and above the wall uses over.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: When you enter the hall, the teachers' table is ______ the stage.
questions.explanation: The table sits at the side of the stage, so we use beside.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: Our house stands ______ a small wood, so we hear birdsong every morning.
questions.explanation: Being close to the wood explains the birdsong, so we use near.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The prize cup was placed ______ the two large vases on the shelf.
questions.explanation: The cup is in the middle of the two vases, so we use between.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: A thick blanket of snow lay ______ the whole football field.
questions.explanation: The snow covers the area above the field, so we use over.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The old cat likes to sleep ______ the warm oven in winter.
questions.explanation: The cat rests at the side of the oven for warmth, so we use beside.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The playground is ______ the swimming pool; we can see it from the changing rooms.
questions.explanation: Being close enough to see the pool shows the playground is near.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: There is a narrow lane ______ the two rows of old shophouses.
questions.explanation: The lane runs in the space separating the two rows, so we use between.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: Mum pulled a blanket ______ the sleeping child to keep her warm.
questions.explanation: The blanket is drawn above and across the child, so we use over.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: We held a large plastic sheet ______ our heads as we ran through the rain.
questions.explanation: The sheet is held above the heads as cover, so we use over.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: The missing key slipped ______ the cupboard and the wall.
questions.explanation: The key falls into the gap separating the cupboard and the wall, so we use between.
questions.subtopic: beside / next to / between / near / over

questions.questionText: A lion is ______ than a house cat.
questions.explanation: Comparing two things uses the comparative; 'big' doubles the final consonant: bigger.

questions.questionText: The elephant is the ______ animal on land.
questions.explanation: Among all land animals we use the superlative: biggest.

questions.questionText: My brother is two years ______ than me.
questions.explanation: 'Than' signals a comparative; comparing ages uses older.

questions.questionText: This is the ______ film I have ever seen!
questions.explanation: 'I have ever seen' covers a whole group, so we use the irregular superlative best.

questions.questionText: Today is ______ than yesterday.
questions.explanation: Comparing two days uses the comparative; 'hot' doubles the final consonant: hotter.

questions.questionText: July is usually the ______ month of the year here.
questions.explanation: Among all months of the year we use the superlative: hottest.

questions.questionText: A newly sharpened knife is ______ than an old one.
questions.explanation: Comparing two knives uses the comparative: sharper.

questions.questionText: Which is the ______ river in the world?
questions.explanation: Among all rivers in the world we use the superlative: longest.

questions.questionText: This storybook is ______ than that one.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives form the comparative with more, so more interesting.

questions.questionText: That was the ______ day of our whole holiday.
questions.explanation: Among all holiday days we use the superlative with most: most exciting.

questions.questionText: My grandmother's soup tastes ______ than the restaurant's.
questions.explanation: 'Than' signals a comparative, and the irregular comparative of good is better.

questions.questionText: The accident was ______ than we first thought.
questions.explanation: 'Than' signals a comparative, and the irregular comparative of bad is worse.

questions.questionText: This is the ______ cake I have ever eaten.
questions.explanation: 'I have ever eaten' covers a whole group, so we use the superlative best.

questions.questionText: A car is usually ______ than a bicycle.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives form the comparative with more, so more expensive.

questions.questionText: Of all the runners in the race, the one from Class Five ran the ______.
questions.explanation: Among all the runners we use the superlative: fastest.

questions.questionText: The weather this week is ______ than last week.
questions.explanation: 'Than' signals a comparative; 'dry' changes y to i: drier.

questions.questionText: This painting is the ______ one in the whole gallery.
questions.explanation: Among all paintings we use the superlative with most: most valuable.

questions.questionText: My room is ______ than my sister's room.
questions.explanation: 'Than' signals a comparative; 'tidy' changes y to i: tidier.

questions.questionText: The exam was ______ than I expected.
questions.explanation: 'Than' signals a comparative; 'easy' changes y to i: easier.

questions.questionText: Which school subject do you think is the ______?
questions.explanation: Choosing the top one among all subjects uses the superlative with most: most difficult.

questions.questionText: Of the two routes home, this one is ______.
questions.explanation: With only two items we use the comparative, not the superlative: shorter.

questions.questionText: After the storm, the country road became ______ than before.
questions.explanation: 'Than' signals a comparative; 'muddy' changes y to i: muddier.

questions.questionText: My cough is getting ______, so I must see a doctor.
questions.explanation: A change towards a lower state uses the irregular comparative worse.

questions.questionText: Which of the two dresses do you like ______?
questions.explanation: Choosing between two things uses the comparative better, not the superlative best.

questions.questionText: The ______ moment of our trip was when we reached the mountain top.
questions.explanation: Among all moments of the trip we use the superlative; 'happy' changes y to i: happiest.

questions.questionText: I saw ______ enormous elephant at the zoo yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Enormous' begins with a vowel sound, so we use an.

questions.questionText: My father works as ______ engineer.
questions.explanation: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so we use an.

questions.questionText: There is ______ orange on the kitchen table.
questions.explanation: 'Orange' begins with a vowel sound, so we use an.

questions.questionText: She drew ______ large circle on the paper.
questions.explanation: 'Large' begins with a consonant sound, so we use a.

questions.questionText: We waited for ______ hour at the railway station.
questions.explanation: 'Hour' has a silent h and begins with a vowel sound, so we use an.

questions.questionText: Please open ______ window; it is very hot in here.
questions.explanation: A specific window in this room is understood by both speakers, so we use the.

questions.questionText: ______ sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: Unique things like the sun take the definite article The.

questions.questionText: He is ______ honest boy; he always tells the truth.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' has a silent h and begins with a vowel sound, so we use an.

questions.questionText: There is ______ new university on the hill.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a /j/ consonant sound, so we use a.

questions.questionText: My mother bought ______ umbrella from the market.
questions.explanation: 'Umbrella' begins with a vowel sound, so we use an.

questions.questionText: I looked ______ for my keys before finding them in my bag.
questions.explanation: Searching in all places uses the place adverb everywhere.

questions.questionText: We ______ have breakfast at seven before going to school.
questions.explanation: Showing how often we eat breakfast uses the frequency adverb usually.

questions.questionText: The children are playing ______ in the garden, not inside the house.
questions.explanation: The contrast with 'inside the house' names the place: outside.

questions.questionText: My little brother ______ eats his vegetables; he always pushes them aside.
questions.explanation: 'Always pushes them aside' means he eats them zero times, so the frequency adverb is never.

questions.questionText: Come ______ and see what I have found.
questions.explanation: The speaker indicates the place where the listener should come, so we use here.

questions.questionText: The morning train arrives ______ at seven o'clock, so we are never late.
questions.explanation: 'We are never late' shows the arrival happens every time, so the frequency adverb is always.

questions.questionText: Please put the wet umbrella ______ by the door, not on the mat.
questions.explanation: The blank tells us where to put the umbrella, so we need an adverb of place: outside.

questions.questionText: My grandmother ______ drinks tea in the evening, usually about once or twice a week.
questions.explanation: 'Once or twice a week' is infrequent but not zero, so the frequency adverb is occasionally.

questions.questionText: Come ______ and warm your hands by the fire.
questions.explanation: The sentence asks the listener to move to the place of the fire, so we use the place adverb near.

questions.questionText: We ______ go to the beach on public holidays; the car park is far too crowded.
questions.explanation: The crowded car park gives a reason for not going, so the frequency adverb is rarely.

questions.questionText: Which sentence gives a direct instruction?
questions.explanation: 'Open the window, please' begins with the base verb and gives a command — an imperative sentence.

questions.questionText: ______ quietly in the library; others are reading.
questions.explanation: An imperative command uses the base form of the verb, so we use Walk.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a polite instruction?

options.label: C
options.text: Please tie your shoelaces before running.

questions.explanation: 'Please tie your shoelaces' gives a direction with the base verb — a polite imperative.

questions.questionText: To switch off the machine, ______ the red button firmly for three seconds.
questions.explanation: Instructions in a procedure use the base verb, so the imperative is press.

questions.questionText: Which sentence tells someone what NOT to do?

options.label: A
options.text: Do not lean out of the window.

questions.explanation: 'Do not lean out of the window' is a negative command — a negative imperative.

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence that uses the speech marks correctly.
questions.explanation: The exact spoken words 'I am hungry' must sit inside a pair of speech marks; only option A closes them properly.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence with the correct commas in a list.

options.label: A
options.text: We bought apples bananas, grapes and oranges.

options.label: B
options.text: We bought apples, bananas, grapes and oranges.

options.label: C
options.text: We bought apples, bananas, grapes, and, oranges.

options.label: D
options.text: We, bought apples, bananas, grapes and oranges.

questions.explanation: Items in a list are separated by commas, with no comma before the first item or between 'and' and the last item.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: "Where are you going?" ______ the teacher. Which word goes after the speech marks?
questions.explanation: After the closing speech marks we still need a full reporting verb; in a narrative past story we use asked.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: Arun said "The bus is late again".

options.label: B
options.text: Arun, said "The bus is late again."

options.label: C
options.text: Arun said, the bus is late again.

options.label: D
options.text: Arun said, "The bus is late again."

questions.explanation: A comma follows the reporting clause, and the full stop sits inside the closing speech marks.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Which list sentence is punctuated correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: On the wall hung a clock, a mirror and two pictures.

options.label: B
options.text: On the wall, hung a clock, a mirror and two pictures.

options.label: C
options.text: On the wall hung a clock a mirror and two pictures.

options.label: D
options.text: On the wall hung, a clock, a mirror, and two pictures.

questions.explanation: The three objects are a list, so commas separate 'clock' and 'mirror' only; no comma after 'hung'.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: "Pass the salt, please," ______ Father.
questions.explanation: The reported speech in a story uses the past-tense reporting verb said.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence with correct list commas.

options.label: A
options.text: My bag contains a notebook, two pens, a ruler, and, an eraser.

options.label: B
options.text: My bag contains a notebook two pens a ruler and an eraser.

options.label: C
options.text: My bag contains a notebook, two pens, a ruler and an eraser.

options.label: D
options.text: My, bag contains a notebook, two pens, a ruler and an eraser.

questions.explanation: Commas separate the listed items; there is no extra comma around 'and' and no comma after the subject.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: "Watch out for the step!" ______ the lifeguard.
questions.explanation: An exclamation inside speech marks is reported with the past-tense verb shouted.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Which sentence places the comma correctly after the reporting clause?

options.label: A
options.text: Mei asked, "Can I borrow your pencil?"

options.label: B
options.text: Mei, asked "Can I borrow your pencil?"

options.label: C
options.text: Mei asked "Can I borrow your pencil?",

options.label: D
options.text: Mei asked "Can I borrow your pencil?"

questions.explanation: The comma comes after 'asked' and before the opening speech marks, and the question mark sits inside them.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: "No, thank you," ______ Arun politely.
questions.explanation: The reported speech in a story uses the past-tense reporting verb replied.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Choose the correctly punctuated direct speech.

options.label: A
options.text: "Thank you for helping me" said the boy.

options.label: B
options.text: Thank you for helping me, said the boy.

options.label: C
options.text: "Thank you for helping me, said the boy."

options.label: D
options.text: "Thank you for helping me," said the boy.

questions.explanation: The spoken words end with a comma inside the opening quotes, then 'said the boy' follows; the quotes wrap only the speech.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Which list needs NO comma because it is only two items?

options.label: B
options.text: I bought bread, milk, eggs and cheese.

options.label: C
options.text: We saw cats, dogs, rabbits and birds.

options.label: D
options.text: She packed a shirt, a skirt, socks and a towel.

questions.explanation: A list of just two items joined by 'and' takes no comma; the other sentences list three or more items.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Choose the sentence that correctly combines a list and direct speech.

options.label: A
options.text: "I need paper, glue, scissors, and string" said the pupil.

options.label: B
options.text: I need paper, glue, scissors and string, said "the pupil".

options.label: C
options.text: "I need paper, glue, scissors and string," said the pupil.

options.label: D
options.text: "I need paper glue scissors and string," said the pupil.

questions.explanation: The list needs commas between items, and the whole spoken sentence sits inside one pair of speech marks.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: "Be careful, the soup ______ very hot," warned Mother.
questions.explanation: Inside the direct speech, 'the soup' is singular, so the verb is is.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Which sentence has a comma in the RIGHT place when the speech comes first?

options.label: D
options.text: Good morning," said the head teacher."

questions.explanation: When the reported clause follows the speech, a comma ends the spoken words inside the quotes, before 'said'.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: In this list, where should the LAST comma go? 'We packed tents, sleeping bags torches and food.'
questions.explanation: The missing comma separates the second and third list items, between 'bags' and 'torches'.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: "Have you ______ your homework yet?" the teacher asked.
questions.explanation: The direct question uses the present perfect 'Have you finished', so the spoken line keeps finished.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Choose the fully correct punctuation of a list inside direct speech.

options.label: A
options.text: "We saw monkeys, snakes, parrots, and, lizards" said the guide.

options.label: B
options.text: "We saw monkeys snakes parrots and lizards" said the guide.

options.label: C
options.text: We saw monkeys, snakes, parrots and lizards," said "the guide."

options.label: D
options.text: "We saw monkeys, snakes, parrots and lizards," said the guide.

questions.explanation: List commas separate the four animals, the full sentence sits inside one quote pair, and the comma falls inside the closing quote.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: "I can't find ______ hat," said Linh, turning the room upside down.
questions.explanation: Inside the direct speech the hat belongs to the speaker, so the possessive determiner my is correct.
questions.subtopic: speech markers (quotation marks) and commas in lists

questions.questionText: Which sentence shows a question INSIDE speech marks correctly?

options.label: A
options.text: "Why is the sky blue," asked the small child?

options.label: B
options.text: "Why is the sky blue?" asked the small child.

options.label: C
options.text: Why is the sky blue?" asked the small child."

options.label: D
options.text: "Why is the sky blue?", asked the small child.

questions.explanation: The question mark belongs to the spoken question and goes inside the closing speech marks, before the reporting clause.

questions.questionText: Rina was ______ to see her old friend at the bus stop. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling of the feeling word is happy; the others are common misspellings.

questions.questionText: We were ______ tired after the long walk up the hill. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The word meaning 'quite' is spelled very, with one r.

questions.questionText: Please ______ the door quietly when you leave. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The verb for shutting a door is close; cloze is a reading exercise, not a verb.

questions.questionText: The baby began to ______ when she saw the doctor. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The base verb is cry; the other forms are not standard English.

questions.questionText: It is ______ to bring a raincoat today; the sky is grey. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The word meaning 'sensible' is spelled wise.

questions.questionText: We sat on the ______ and watched the sunset. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The sandy place by the sea is the beach; beech is a type of tree.

questions.questionText: The old clock ______ loudly all night. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: Past tense of tick is ticked, with -ed.

questions.questionText: Put the return ______ in your pocket so you do not lose it. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The card for travel or entry is spelled ticket.

questions.questionText: The children laughed at the ______ clown. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The word for 'amusing' is funny, doubling the final consonant + y.

questions.questionText: We heard a strange ______ from the attic. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: An unwanted sound is a noise; 'oi' is the correct spelling.

questions.questionText: The farmer keeps his sheep in the ______. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The open grassy area is a field; remember 'i before e' here.

questions.questionText: Please ______ your name at the top of the page. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The verb for forming letters is write; rite is a ceremony.

questions.questionText: The kite flew high ______ the trees. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The BrE preposition meaning higher than is above.

questions.questionText: We bought a ______ of bread from the baker. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: A single unit of bread is a loaf; the plural would be loaves.

questions.questionText: The bus was late, ______ we arrived just in time. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The joining word showing contrast is but.

questions.questionText: My little sister is ______ afraid of the dark. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The adverb is really (real + ly), not 'reely'.

questions.questionText: We had to ______ for the bus in the rain. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: To stay until something comes is wait; weight is how heavy something is.

questions.questionText: The magician pulled a rabbit out of his ______. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The magician's rabbit comes from a hat; hate is a feeling.

questions.questionText: There are seven days in a ______. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: Seven days is a week; weak means not strong.

questions.questionText: Please do not ______ on the grass; the seeds are growing. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: To move on foot is walk; the l-k spelling is correct.

questions.questionText: We keep our toys in a big wooden ______. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: A storage container is a box; the plural is boxes.

questions.questionText: The fire ______ quickly through the dry leaves. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: Past tense of spread is spread (unchanged), not 'spred'.

questions.questionText: She put on her coat ______ it was cold outside. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The reason word is because — 'be-cause', a common misspelling trap.

questions.questionText: The two friends sat ______ on the bench and talked. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The word meaning 'with each other' is together.

questions.questionText: We ______ a strange noise during the night. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: Past tense of hear is heard; a herd is a group of animals.

questions.questionText: The clown made the children ______. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The verb is laugh, with 'au'.

questions.questionText: It is important to eat ______ food every day. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: Healthy = health + y, keeping the 'al'.

questions.questionText: We had to ______ the old vase very carefully. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The base verb is carry; in a sentence like this (after 'to') the simple form is carry.

questions.questionText: The ______ of the mountain was covered in snow. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The highest point is the top; no final -e and no doubled p.

questions.questionText: She ______ the window because the room was hot. Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: Past tense of open is opened (add -ed, no doubled n).

questions.questionText: A note stuck to a bottle reads: "FRAGILE — THIS SIDE UP." What is its purpose?

options.label: A
options.text: To tell people how to handle the box

questions.explanation: A handling label like 'FRAGILE — THIS SIDE UP' exists to tell carriers how to treat the parcel.

questions.questionText: A yellow sign on the school gate says: "NO ENTRY — STAFF ONLY." What does it mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Pupils may play at the gate

options.label: B
options.text: Pupils must not go through that gate

options.label: D
options.text: The gate is open to everyone

questions.explanation: 'NO ENTRY — STAFF ONLY' is a notice telling pupils not to use that entrance.

questions.questionText: Linh leaves a message on her brother's desk: "Mum called — dinner at seven." Why did she write it?

options.label: A
options.text: To invite him to a party

options.label: C
options.text: To pass on information she heard

questions.explanation: The note is a short message passing on a piece of news (the dinner time) he would otherwise miss.

questions.questionText: A card pinned to a potted plant says: "WATER ME TWICE A WEEK." What kind of text is this?
questions.explanation: Words stuck onto an object to tell you what to do with it are an instructional label.

questions.questionText: A sign at the bus stop reads: "BUS 120 — TAKING 20 MINUTES LONGER." What is its purpose?

options.label: A
options.text: To warn passengers of a delay

questions.explanation: A notice at a stop about delay time exists to inform/warn passengers.

questions.questionText: A small note in a library book says: "Due back Friday 12 June." This is most like ______.
questions.explanation: A due-date note reminds the reader of a deadline — when the item must be returned.

questions.questionText: A paper taped to the classroom door reads: "Class 5A — MOVE TO ROOM 10 TODAY." Who wrote this, and why?

options.label: B
options.text: A parent, to ask a question

options.label: C
options.text: A teacher, to tell pupils where to go

questions.explanation: A room-change notice on a door is written by staff to direct pupils.

questions.questionText: A message reads: "Sorry I missed your call — will ring back after practice." What is the writer doing?

options.label: D
options.text: Explaining and promising a later contact

questions.explanation: The note apologises for a missed call and says the writer will ring later — a message to keep in touch.

questions.questionText: A sign on a pond reads: "DO NOT FEED THE DUCKS." The main purpose is to ______.
questions.explanation: A sign telling people what not to do is a rule or warning notice.

questions.questionText: A label on a medicine bottle reads: "SHAKE WELL BEFORE USE." This tells the reader to ______.

options.label: B
options.text: do something before taking the medicine

questions.explanation: A use-instruction label tells you an action to perform before using the product.

questions.questionText: A notice on the canteen door reads: "TODAY'S SPECIAL — FRIED RICE RM6." What kind of text is it?

options.label: C
options.text: A notice advertising a daily offer

questions.explanation: A posted board listing a price and a dish is a notice advertising an offer.

questions.questionText: A short note to a friend says: "Bring your old storybooks — we are donating them." The writer mainly wants to ______.

options.label: D
options.text: remind the friend to bring something

questions.explanation: The message's aim is to remind the friend to bring books for the donation.

questions.questionText: A sticker on an electrical plug reads: "240 VOLTS — FOR ADULT USE ONLY." Why is this label here?
questions.explanation: Voltage and 'adult use only' on an appliance is a safety warning label.

questions.questionText: A pinned notice says: "LOST: A blue water bottle, lunchtime, near the field." The writer wants to ______.

options.label: B
options.text: ask for help finding something lost

questions.explanation: A 'LOST' notice asks the public to help return a missing item.

questions.questionText: A note inside a packed lunchbox reads: "Hope you feel better soon — love, Mum." What is the writer's main aim?
questions.explanation: A loving get-well message in a lunchbox exists to cheer someone up — a caring personal message.

questions.questionText: Read: "Linh tucked the shivering kitten into her coat and carried it all the way home." From this, Linh is shown to be ______.
questions.explanation: Sheltering a cold kitten and walking it home shows Linh is kind and caring.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "The old lighthouse stood on a rocky cliff, and gulls cried above the grey sea." When and where is this scene most likely set?

options.label: B
options.text: At the seaside, by the sea

questions.explanation: A lighthouse, cliff, gulls and sea all point to a seaside setting.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "Arun shared his last biscuit with the new boy, who had no one to sit with." The story shows the value of ______.
questions.explanation: Giving away his own last biscuit to a lonely newcomer shows the value of sharing.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "Every morning, before the sun rose, Grandma watered her plants on the wooden veranda." The scene happens ______.
questions.explanation: 'Before the sun rose' tells us the action happens early in the morning.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "Bo wiped the table without being asked, then helped his little sister with her shoes." Bo is best described as ______.
questions.explanation: Doing chores and helping a sibling unasked shows Bo is helpful.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "The market woke at dawn: baskets of fish, baskets of mangoes, and vendors calling across the lane." This story is set ______.
questions.explanation: Vendors, baskets of produce and calling across a lane all describe a busy open-air market.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "Although Rina was afraid of heights, she held the rope tightly and climbed to ring the old bell." Rina shows ______.
questions.explanation: Doing something frightening on purpose, gripping the rope and climbing, shows courage.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "Mei kept the seed in her pocket for weeks, checking it each night before she planted it in the tin can." The story suggests Mei feels ______ about the seed.
questions.explanation: Keeping and checking the seed nightly, then planting it gently, shows hope and care.

questions.questionText: Read: "The train hissed into the foggy station, its windows streaked with rain." What time and weather does this describe?

options.label: A
options.text: A misty, rainy day at a station

questions.explanation: Fog, a hissing train and rain-streaked windows describe a misty, rainy day at a station.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "Arun found a wallet full of money on the bench. He handed it straight to the policeman." The value shown here is ______.
questions.explanation: Turning in a found wallet instead of keeping it shows honesty.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "The lanterns glowed red over the narrow street, where dancers balanced dragons on sticks." This festival is most likely set ______.

options.label: A
options.text: in an empty school at noon

options.label: B
options.text: on a farm in the morning

options.label: C
options.text: in a town at a night-time celebration

questions.explanation: Red lanterns, a narrow street and dragon dancers describe a night-time street festival.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "Linh practised the violin every evening, even when her fingers ached, until the tune was perfect." Linh shows the value of ______.
questions.explanation: Keeping up practice through discomfort until success shows determination.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "When the new pupil sat alone at lunch, Bo carried his tray over and smiled." Which value best fits Bo's action?
questions.explanation: Sitting with a lonely newcomer and smiling reaches out in friendship.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "The storm knocked down their hut, but the villagers shared their roofs, their food and their blankets until the sun returned." The main value of the story is ______.

options.label: B
options.text: working together to help one another

questions.explanation: Villagers sharing shelter and food after a disaster shows community and mutual help.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values

questions.questionText: Read: "Every autumn, the old fisherman repaired his nets at dusk on the same wooden jetty, watching the boats come home." Which detail tells us this happens at a FIXED place over many years?

options.label: C
options.text: He returns to the same jetty every autumn at dusk

questions.explanation: 'Every autumn' and 'the same wooden jetty' show a repeated, fixed place and time over years.
questions.subtopic: respond to literary texts: characters / place and time / values
